contribution.position: My reliability position is unchanged. The perf report shows cold_start at 1900ms at peak load against an 800ms budget, about 2.4x over. The QA turn cites 600ms from the same report, which looks like a different load condition. Peak is the condition that matters for a cache warmer, so the 600ms figure does not offset the peak result unless someone shows it was measured at peak. The incident log shows two sev2 incidents last quarter, both from retry storms. A slow cold start at peak can trigger retries, so the known failure mode may be amplified. The test report (412 passed, 87% coverage) covers functional correctness, not peak-load or retry behavior. The runbook's rollback lowers recovery cost but does not prevent the failure. Needed for this axis to move: (1) a peak-load test with cold_start inside 800ms, or a documented waiver for the overage; (2) evidence of retry and backoff behavior under peak load that rules out a repeat of the retry storms; (3) a reconciliation of the 600ms and 1900ms figures. The cost and operability findings are not in dispute and do not touch this gap.
